_README: Differences between a rebuild and the delivered datasets that are KNOWN, measured and
explained. compare.py reports these separately from new ones, so its exit code answers
'did anything change that we cannot account for?' rather than 'is every byte equal?',
which no rebuild of a GPU pipeline can be.
Each key is '<family>:<dataset>/<path>' and each value says why. A pattern may end in
'*' to cover a family of paths. Nothing is tolerated silently: an entry here is a claim
that someone measured the difference and found its cause, and the summary names any
entry that stopped matching, so an explanation cannot be inherited after it stops
being true. That report covers only the datasets the invocation compared -- the three
families run as separate jobs, and judging all of them in each one listed 7 to 9
entries as stale per run, every one of them live in a sibling job.
A key beginning '_' is prose, not an entry: it is where a cause shared by many paths
is written once, so the entries can cite it instead of repeating it.
Measured on the clean-tree run of 2026-11-08; see README section 7.
sthelar:lung_s3/hovernet.json: 170,794 cells against 171,239, which is 0.26% and past what this backend's noise explains (ovary_s1 and skin_s4 come back +7 of 317,764 and +8 of 98,678, and the 'segment_amp' policy calls both equal). lung_s3's outlier is a tissue-mask boundary difference -- its he.tiff is pixel-equal and 90% of the disputed cells sit within 1% of an image edge against 1.1% for cells in general, and the disputed strip is blank paper -- and the original mask was never delivered, so the two cannot be compared.
sthelar:*/image_dict.pt: One crop per HoVerNet cell, so its key set is exactly hovernet.json's and it differs by the same cells. Shapes all (3, 64, 64) and the reference's keys are all present on ovary_s1 and skin_s4.
sthelar:*/hoptimus_tile_embed_bench_*.pt: One embedding per HoVerNet cell; same cause as image_dict.pt. Shapes all (1536,).
sthelar:*/spot_dict.json: spot -> cells, so a cell gained or lost at the tissue border changes that spot's count: 9 of 1,646 spots on skin_s4, 17 of 5,431 on ovary_s1, 54 of 3,560 on lung_s3 plus 4 spots lung_s3 does not reach. The proportions built from these spots are nonetheless bit-identical at all five levels.
xenium:lung/sim_Xenium_V1_humanLung_Canc: 9 of 107,286 position-paired rows differ, each by a single type flip, on nuclei whose contour moved under HoVerNet's run-to-run variation. All 141,257 nuclei pair within 1 px.
xenium:lung/spot_dict_real.json: All 1,957 delivered spots are present; one extra spot holds a single nucleus, which is one of the 31 nuclei HoVerNet places differently. 1,928 of the 1,957 hold the same cells.
xenium:lung/sim_Xenium_V1_humanLung_Canc: The same 1,957 spots plus the one extra; 98.93% of the shared proportion rows are identical, the rest being spots whose membership changed by one nucleus.
xenium:lung/pseudo_adata_real.h5ad: The same 1,957 spots plus the one extra. Same cause as spot_dict_real.json.
xenium:breast/*: Breast is rebuilt from the UNCROPPED H&E pyramid (24241 x 30786) where the delivered dataset used a 20511 x 27587 crop recorded nowhere but in a re-fitted affine. HoVerNet sees more tissue and finds 170,888 nuclei against 175,204, so every file is ~2.5% smaller in cell count and the ids do not correspond: 2,656 spots against 2,651, 116,752 ground-truth rows against 120,336. This is a whole-slide wildcard and so gives up on catching a NEW breast regression here -- what guards breast instead is its own `verify` stage, which checks the type-code contract, the column order the palette is zipped against, the ground truth being exactly the coded nuclei, the embeddings covering exactly the ground truth, and the spot count against `delivered_spots` within 1%. It passes with zero issues. See README section 4.
visiumhd:*/plots/05_gallery_lv*.png: Example nucleus crops, chosen by sampling the cell table. The delivered galleries were drawn from bin2cell's original cell numbering; a rebuild renumbers, so different nuclei are shown. The choice is taken from a spatial sort now, so two rebuilds agree with each other even though neither matches the delivered figure.
visiumhd:*/plots/07_matching.png: The figure is sized to the text of the matching-check report, and this pipeline runs 11 checks where the original ran 12 -- it dropped the soft file-mtime check. 17 px of height, one line of monospace text.
_P2: P2's residuals all have one cause, measured: of its 283,047 annotated cells, 1,862
(0.66%) land on a nucleus the fresh bin2cell/HoVerNet pass segmented differently, so
the centroid re-key cannot carry their labels and they are dropped. They are not
tolerance-boundary cases -- the nearest fresh nucleus is a median 1.49 px away (p90
5.9, max 26.4), where a cell that merely jittered sits at 0.0004 px -- and loosening
CENTROID_ATOL does not recover them: 2 px would add 1,201 while the 5 px-shifted
control starts accepting 37 matches it must reject. So 0.66% of P2's cells are
genuinely gone from the rebuild, and everything keyed on cells carries that forward.
P5 loses none, which is what says this is P2's segmentation and not the method.
visiumhd:P2/hovernet.json: 280,600 nuclei against 282,462, which is the 1,862 unmatched annotated cells (see _P2) minus the 585 unassigned ones both builds remove. The segmentation itself reproduces: metadata records 290,840 nuclei found against 290,829, 0.004% apart.
visiumhd:P2/spot_dict.json: 3,562 spots against 3,564, with 0 extra; 3,266 of the 3,562 hold the same number of cells. The two missing spots held only cells from the 1,862 (see _P2), and a spot that lost one of them changes its count.
visiumhd:P2/pseudovisium.h5ad: The same 3,562 spots of 3,564. Same cause as spot_dict.json.
visiumhd:P2/sim/cell_types.csv: 7 of 280,574 position-paired cells sit in a different spot. Those nuclei moved by under 1 px, which is enough to cross a honeycomb boundary when they were already on one; all three level labels and the hovernet type agree on every paired cell.
visiumhd:P2/sim/proportions_lv*.csv: The same 3,562 spots of 3,564, and 94-96% of the shared rows identical -- a spot that lost one of the 1,862 cells (see _P2) has a different denominator, so its proportions move.
visiumhd:P2/plots/01_overview_*.png: A scatter of every cell over the capture area; 0.66% of the cells are absent (see _P2) and matplotlib's point rendering differs wherever one was, which is 14-18% of the pixels inside the axes.
visiumhd:P2/plots/04_dominant_lv*.png: Per-spot dominant type over the same scatter. Same cause as 01_overview_*.png.
visiumhd:P2/plots/06_spot_qc.png: Histograms of cells and counts per spot, drawn from the cell table that is short by 0.66% (see _P2).
visiumhd:P2/metadata.json: The 'metadata' policy compares the data paths, not the provenance, and on P2 those counts are lower by exactly the 1,862 cells of _P2: cells_annotated 281,185 vs 283,047, nuclei_written 280,600 vs 282,462, and 3,562 spots vs 3,564. P5 agrees on every data path, which is what says the policy is measuring something.
